#222 correctness review, round 1: BLOCK

Exact head: `992fd0a1b55e95843550dc5fc6d3475e4bac4611`.

**F001: a previously registered standby still reaches host proof on every retry.** The new early brake runs only when the incoming claim already has `supersedes` (`crates/daemon/src/registration.rs:499-514`). A normal session that previously held an address sends its own old ID without that field: `chooseRegistration` prefers its same-session candidate, even when tombstoned, and sets `replacing = false` (`.copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:384-445`).

Concrete sequence: session A registers; session B's newer prompt takes the same-process seat and retires A's row; A's still-running extension retries with A's ID and no `supersedes`. The early brake cannot match. `verify_native_host` runs (`registration.rs:516-525`), and only afterward `register_inner` infers B as the predecessor (`:817-835`) and returns `NativeHolderCurrent` under the lock (`:1008-1019`). The existing `new_session_takes_the_seat_on_its_first_prompt_and_the_old_chat_stands_by` case uses precisely that old-ID/no-supersedes claim.

Thus a bounce alone does not remove the process-proof cost for previously active standby sessions on old extensions; new extensions still pay it for their eventual ten-minute checks. The new zero-process-read test covers only a blank session with explicit `supersedes`, not this common path. This misses F162's principal resource-cost requirement.

Fix: resolve the same eligible current-holder candidate before host proof for both explicit and inferred predecessors, reusing the existing resolution rules rather than adding a second divergent policy. Keep it refusal-only and retain the full proof/locked checks for any admitted registration. Extend the observer-count regression with a retired old session that retries its own ID without `supersedes`; assert zero proof reads while the holder is current and successful proof/admission when takeover is eligible.

The implemented early return is otherwise a one-direction safety brake: removing it adds proof work before the same refusal, never authority to register. The extension's three-refusal threshold, 30-second/ten-minute selection, prompt/live-resume re-arm, history-resume exclusion, success clear and abortable waits match the requested state machine. Existing host and receiver-lease admission checks remain.
